summary: PR #1 adds a useful --output-dir CLI option to override the default report directory, with proper backward compatibility. However, the implementation has significant quality and security concerns. The most critical issue is a HIGH severity path traversal vulnerability where user-provided paths are not validated, potentially allowing writes to arbitrary filesystem locations. Additionally, the core precedence logic (--output-dir > REPORTS_DIR > 'reports') has zero test coverage, and edge cases like empty strings, duplicate arguments, and cross-platform paths are untested. The code would benefit from extracting hardcoded values to constants, separating validation concerns, and simplifying verbose patterns. Overall score: 55/100 (Code Quality: 65, Test Coverage: 25, Refactoring: 75). Recommend addressing the security vulnerability and adding comprehensive tests before merging.

analyzers.summary: PR #1 adds a per-run --output-dir CLI option to override the default reports directory. The implementation is mostly sound with good backward compatibility and type safety. However, there is a HIGH severity security issue: the output directory path is not validated, creating a path traversal risk where arbitrary filesystem locations could be written to. Additionally, test coverage is incomplete for the new feature's edge cases and precedence rules.

findings.title: Path Traversal Vulnerability - Unvalidated Output Directory
findings.description: The --output-dir parameter accepts arbitrary filesystem paths without validation or sanitization. An attacker or misconfigured script could specify paths like '../../../etc' or absolute paths to sensitive system directories. The value flows directly from user input through parseArguments() to resolve() and then to ReportGenerator.generate(), which creates directories and writes files. While Node.js filesystem permissions provide some protection, this violates the principle of least privilege and could lead to unintended file writes, data leakage, or denial of service if sensitive directories are targeted.
findings.recommendation: Add path validation before accepting the output directory. Consider: (1) Resolve the path and verify it's within an allowed directory tree (e.g., project root or designated reports folder), (2) Reject paths containing '..' after normalization that escape the boundary, (3) Use an allowlist approach if only specific output locations are valid, (4) Add a security boundary check function that validates the resolved path stays within acceptable bounds. Example: After resolve(), check if the normalized path starts with an approved prefix.

findings.title: Missing Input Validation for Output Directory Path
findings.description: Unlike --owner and --repo parameters which have regex validation (/^[\w.-]+$/), the --output-dir parameter has no character, format, or safety validation. This inconsistency makes the code vulnerable to unexpected filesystem behavior, especially on Windows where reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) can cause issues, or when paths contain invalid characters.
findings.recommendation: Add validation for the --output-dir value similar to other parameters. Check for: (1) Maximum path length (e.g., 255 or platform-specific limits), (2) Invalid filesystem characters, (3) Windows reserved names if cross-platform support is needed, (4) Null bytes or other injection patterns. Consider adding a validatePath() helper function that can be reused.

findings.title: Incomplete Test Coverage for New Feature
findings.description: The new test case 'accepts a per-run report output directory' only validates that the argument parser correctly extracts the --output-dir value. It does not test: (1) Precedence when both --output-dir and REPORTS_DIR environment variable are set, (2) Actual file writing behavior to the custom directory, (3) Error handling when the directory cannot be created, (4) Path normalization across platforms, (5) Validation and rejection of invalid or dangerous paths.
findings.recommendation: Add comprehensive test cases including: (1) Test that --output-dir takes precedence over REPORTS_DIR environment variable, (2) Integration test verifying files are written to the custom directory, (3) Test error handling when mkdir fails (permission denied, invalid path, etc.), (4) Test path normalization behavior, (5) Test rejection of invalid paths (if validation is added as recommended), (6) Test with both relative and absolute paths to document expected behavior.

findings.title: Inconsistent Spread Operator Pattern
findings.description: The code uses a conditional spread operator to optionally include outputDirectory: `...(outputDirectory ? { outputDirectory } : {})`. While functionally correct, this pattern is less readable than simply always including the optional field. TypeScript's optional properties allow undefined values, so `outputDirectory` could be included unconditionally.
findings.recommendation: Simplify to: `return { owner, repo, prNumber, outputDirectory };` since the interface already declares outputDirectory as optional (`outputDirectory?: string`). This is clearer and more consistent with TypeScript conventions. The value will be `undefined` if not provided, which is semantically correct.
findings.codeExample:
const outputDirectory = values.get('--output-dir');
return { owner, repo, prNumber, ...(outputDirectory ? { outputDirectory } : {}) };

findings.title: Platform-Specific Test Path
findings.description: The test uses a Windows-style path '.\\review-output' which works on Windows but doesn't document or test cross-platform behavior. The codebase uses Node's path.resolve() which should handle this, but the test doesn't verify it.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding test cases with both forward-slash (POSIX-style) and backslash (Windows-style) paths to document expected cross-platform behavior. Alternatively, use path.join() in tests to generate platform-appropriate paths. Add a comment explaining that path.resolve() handles cross-platform normalization.

analyzers.summary: The new --output-dir feature has minimal test coverage (~25%). Only basic argument parsing is tested; the critical precedence logic in runCli (line 70: target.outputDirectory ?? env.REPORTS_DIR ?? 'reports') is completely untested. No edge cases, integration tests, or validation of the precedence behavior exist.

findings.title: Critical: Precedence logic in runCli is completely untested
findings.description: The core functionality of the PR - the precedence rule where --output-dir takes priority over REPORTS_DIR environment variable - is implemented at src/cli.ts:70 but has zero test coverage. The expression `target.outputDirectory ?? env.REPORTS_DIR ?? 'reports'` determines where reports are written, yet no test verifies this three-way fallback behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests for runCli that mock the environment and verify: (1) when both outputDirectory and REPORTS_DIR are set, outputDirectory wins; (2) when only REPORTS_DIR is set, it is used; (3) when neither is set, 'reports' is used. Mock reviewPullRequest and ReportGenerator.generate to isolate the path resolution logic. Verify the resolved absolute path is passed to generate().

findings.title: High: No validation of outputDirectory argument value
findings.description: The parseArguments function accepts any non-empty string for --output-dir without validation. Unlike owner and repo which are validated with regex (line 44), outputDirectory has no checks for empty strings, whitespace-only values, or path traversal attempts. A value like '' or '  ' or '../../../sensitive' would be accepted and passed to path.resolve().
findings.recommendation: Add validation for outputDirectory: reject empty or whitespace-only strings with a clear error message. Consider whether absolute paths should be required or if relative paths should be rejected. Add tests for parseArguments with edge cases: --output-dir '', --output-dir '  ', --output-dir containing only special characters.

findings.title: High: Missing edge case tests for --output-dir parsing
findings.description: The single test added (tests/cli.test.ts:13-22) only covers the happy path with a Windows-style relative path. Critical edge cases are untested: empty string, whitespace-only, missing value (e.g., --output-dir as last argument), duplicate --output-dir flags, argument order variations, absolute vs relative paths, paths with spaces or special characters.
findings.recommendation: Expand the test suite with specific test cases: (1) reject empty --output-dir value; (2) reject whitespace-only value; (3) reject duplicate --output-dir; (4) accept --output-dir in various argument positions; (5) accept absolute and relative paths; (6) accept paths with spaces when quoted.

findings.title: Medium: No test for outputDirectory field omission when not provided
findings.description: Line 51 uses conditional spread `...(outputDirectory ? { outputDirectory } : {})` to omit the field when --output-dir is not provided. While the first test implicitly verifies omission by not including it in the expected object, there's no explicit test documenting this behavior is intentional and important for the precedence logic.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit test case that verifies parseArguments without --output-dir returns an object without the outputDirectory property (using expect(result).not.toHaveProperty('outputDirectory')). This documents the intentional omission that enables the runCli fallback behavior.

findings.title: Medium: Path resolution behavior not tested
findings.description: The runCli function calls resolve() on the chosen directory (line 70), converting relative paths to absolute. The test uses a relative Windows path '.\review-output' but doesn't verify it's resolved to an absolute path. Cross-platform path handling (Windows backslash vs Unix forward slash) is not tested.
findings.recommendation: Add a test for runCli (mocking dependencies) that verifies path.resolve() is called with the correct input and the resolved absolute path is passed to ReportGenerator.generate(). Test both relative and absolute input paths. Consider testing cross-platform path formats.

findings.title: Low: Updated usage message not verified in tests
findings.description: The usage message at line 40 was updated to include [--output-dir <path>] but no test explicitly checks this message content. The existing test only checks the message is thrown on missing arguments (using .toThrow('Usage:')).
findings.recommendation: Update the existing test expectation to verify the complete usage message includes '--output-dir'. Use .toThrow('Usage: npm run dev -- --owner <owner> --repo <repo> --pr-number <number> [--output-dir <path>]') to ensure documentation in error messages stays accurate.

The main opportunities are: extracting hardcoded option lists to constants, simplifying the conditional object spread syntax, and improving test coverage for the output directory resolution precedence. The parseArguments function is growing in complexity and would benefit from extracting validation logic. Overall, the code is well-structured with no critical issues.

findings.title: parseArguments function has multiple responsibilities
findings.description: The parseArguments function handles argument parsing, structural validation, and business rule validation (owner/repo format, PR number range) all in one 39-line function. This reduces readability and makes the function harder to test independently.

findings.title: Magic strings for CLI option names repeated throughout
findings.description: Option names like '--owner', '--repo', '--pr-number', and '--output-dir' are repeated as string literals throughout the parsing and validation logic. This creates risk of typos and makes refactoring harder.

findings.title: Triple nullish coalescing could be more explicit
findings.description: The line `resolve(target.outputDirectory ?? env.REPORTS_DIR ?? 'reports')` chains three fallback values. While functional, it's dense and the precedence logic isn't self-documenting.

testGaps: No test verifies the output directory resolution precedence in runCli
No test validates that --output-dir accepts cross-platform paths correctly

Simplify optional property handling by removing unnecessary conditional spread operator
Consider using a CLI parsing library like 'commander' or 'yargs' for better scalability if more options are planned

recommendations: CRITICAL: Add comprehensive integration tests for the precedence logic (--output-dir > REPORTS_DIR > 'reports') in runCli before merging. Mock dependencies to verify the correct path is resolved and passed to ReportGenerator.generate() in all three scenarios.

MEDIUM: Extract hardcoded CLI option names and validation arrays to module-level constants (CLI_OPTIONS, VALID_OPTIONS) to reduce maintenance burden and prevent typos when adding future options.
